rehearsal_note: Rehearsal for the demo. The decisions and the risk statement were written for practice, not by an accountable owner. Not a real sign-off.
head: 9df83c38409c8bfad0517aebffe48211eda4a5b4

reading_budget.basis: line-level: flagged src/template hunks whole; doc/test hunks only lines near cited evidence gaps

checked.text: For a [MessagePackObject] type whose member is a closed generic value type from a referenced assembly, the analyzer no longer throws IndexOutOfRangeException (AD0001).
For the same input the generator no longer throws (no CS8785) and a GeneratedMessagePackResolver is emitted.

not_checked.what: claim C3: Only struct<T> and record struct<T> from metadata change behaviour; struct, record struct, class<T> and record class<T> from metadata behave exactly as before.
claim C4: No diagnostic that was reported before the change for a type declared in source is lost, moved or changed by the new constructor-level filter.
claim C5: No safety-relevant diagnostic is silently dropped for types the user controls.
claim C6: Diagnostics about the members of a closed generic type from a referenced assembly are reported by the assembly that defines it, so any problem must be fixed there.
claim C7: An unattributed public member of a type defined in a referenced assembly is reported by the project that defines that type.
claim C8: Dropping a diagnostic that has no location in the compilation is required because analyzers are not permitted to report against a location that does not exist.
claim C9: No live DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing remains in TypeCollector.cs; the only remaining occurrence is commented out.
claim C10: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null only for properties that have no source declaration (metadata), so no source-declared property loses its diagnostic.

not_checked.why: no test fails when this code is reverted; owner read it by eye

not_checked.what: the three new tests on the 3.1.x branch
not_checked.why: this branch is based on an older commit and the owner has not rebuilt on master yet

refusal_decisions.question: Do you accept a blanket drop of unlocated diagnostics, or must the drop be limited to symbols that are actually declared in metadata?
refusal_decisions.note: The crash only needs two null-safe lookups. A filter on all 28 call sites can hide a diagnostic nobody planned to hide, and the record case already shows one.

refusal_decisions.question: Is the documented guarantee true for the packages your users reference, and should it say 'may be reported' instead?
refusal_decisions.decision: Soften to 'may be reported by the defining assembly'
refusal_decisions.note: A NuGet package built without our analyzer reports nothing, so the doc sentence promises more than we can check.

refusal_decisions.question: Should a consuming project get at least an informational diagnostic when a referenced generic type has an unattributed public member?
refusal_decisions.decision: Decide later, track in an issue
refusal_decisions.note: Whether consumers get an informational hint is a product call for the maintainers. It should not block the crash fix.

refusal_decisions.question: Which branch does this fix target, and must the new tests be re-run on that branch before you sign?
refusal_decisions.note: The branch sits on an older base. I want the three new tests green on the branch we ship from before this merges.

residual_risk_owner_words: I read the diagnostic filter and the helper by hand. Three tests fail on the old code, so the crash fix is real. What I did not run: the other 3.1.x branch, packages built without the analyzer, and any record shape beyond the three tests. If the filter is wider than it should be, a user could lose a diagnostic and see a clean build, and I accept that until the narrowing lands.
